extracted.intended_audience: Congress, Department of Commerce, USPTO leadership, patent and trademark stakeholders (applicants, examiners, practitioners), and the public
extracted.subtask_description: Agency-level performance, compliance, and operational standards the USPTO uses to evaluate and run its patent and trademark business lines, including strategic goals, performance measures (pendency, quality, compliance), IT and financial management, and legal/administrative controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal I: Optimize Patent Quality and Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Goal I: Optimize Patent Quality and Timeliness (Strategic Goal for Patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives under Goal I include: Optimize Patent Application Pendency; Issue Highly Reliable Patents; Foster Innovation Through Business Effectiveness; Enhance Operations of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB). Resources invested and program costs are tracked against measurable outcomes and targets in the strategic performance framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize Patent Application Pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimize Patent Application Pendency (explicit objective under Goal I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured via first action pendency and total pendency (months) and managed by aligning examination capacity with workloads; part of the Balanced Scorecard and annual performance targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue Highly Reliable Patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue Highly Reliable Patents (explicit objective under Goal I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed through compliance metrics (first action compliance rate, final compliance rate), exceptional office action rates, and quality management activities to ensure issued patents are reliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster Innovation Through Business Effectiveness (Patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foster Innovation Through Business Effectiveness as an objective supporting patent mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes aligning resources, improving processes, and enhancing examiner training and tools to support innovation and business efficiency in patent operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance Operations of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance Operations of the PTAB (explicit objective under Goal I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers improving PTAB timeliness, consistency, and procedures for appeals and post-issuance proceedings; tracked within strategic performance measures and subject to legal developments affecting PTAB authority and reviewability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal II: Optimize Trademark Quality and Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Goal II: Optimize Trademark Quality and Timeliness (Strategic Goal for Trademarks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives under Goal II include: Optimize Trademark Application Pendency; Issue High-Quality Trademarks; Foster Business Effectiveness; Enhance Operations of the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board (TTAB). Metrics such as average first action and total pendency are used to track performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize Trademark Application Pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimize Trademark Application Pendency (explicit objective under Goal II).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured via average first action pendency and average total pendency (months); requires aligning examining attorney capacity with workloads and monitoring e-commerce and filing trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue High-Quality Trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue High-Quality Trademarks (explicit objective under Goal II).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed through examining attorney determinations of registrability, compliance with the Trademark Act, and quality measures such as first action and final compliance rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance Operations of the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board (TTAB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance Operations of the TTAB (explicit objective under Goal II).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes improving TTAB procedures, panel composition, and supervisory processes; informed by litigation and Appointments Clause developments that affect ATJ appointments and Director rehearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal III: Provide Domestic and Global Leadership on IP Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Goal III: Provide Domestic and Global Leadership to Improve Intellectual Property Policy, Enforcement, and Protection Worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives include providing leadership and education on domestic and international IP policy and awareness, and tracked via measures such as progress in prioritized countries and number of trainees on IP best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic Performance Framework and Balanced Scorecard
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a comprehensive Strategic Performance Framework and quarterly Balanced Scorecard to guide and monitor implementation of objectives, initiatives, and performance measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key performance outcome measures (9 for FY2021) and supporting metrics are monitored quarterly; annual performance targets are set for measurable outcomes and presented in public reporting and the Data Visualization Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average First Action Pendency (months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average First Action Pendency (months) — a key performance indicator for examination timeliness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure timeliness of first office action issuance; tracked historically and compared to targets (examples: FY2021 actuals and targets shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: Average Total Pendency (months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average Total Pendency (months) — a key performance indicator for overall time to disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes total months from filing to final disposition; tracked against targets to evaluate overall examination timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Action Compliance Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: First Action Compliance Rate — a quality metric indicating compliance of first office actions with examination standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a percentage (e.g., 97.x% values in tables); used to assess the quality of initial examiner work and to drive quality improvement activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Compliance Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Compliance Rate — a quality metric indicating compliance of final office actions with examination standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a percentage and used alongside first action compliance to assess the reliability of examination outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptional Office Action Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptional Office Action rate — a measure reflecting issuance of exceptional actions by examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracked as a percentage of actions and used to understand examination practices and potential training or policy interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTA (Patent Term Adjustment) Compliance Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Total PTA Compliance - Mailed Actions and Total PTA Compliance - Remaining Inventory — indicators used to monitor compliance with PTA calculations and mailing practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These measures track whether USPTO complies with statutory timing requirements for mailings and inventory, and are reported in the strategic performance tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentage Progress in Prioritized Countries (OPIA measure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of prioritized countries for which IP country teams have made progress on at least three of four performance criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four criteria: institutional improvements in IP office administration; institutional improvements of IP enforcement entities; improvements in IP laws and regulations; establishment of government-to-government cooperative mechanisms. Performance reported as percentages (100% = 3 out of 3 countries; 66% = 2 out of 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number Trained on IP Best Practices (OPIA measure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of people, including foreign government officials and U.S. stakeholders, trained on best practices to protect and enforce IP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to quantify capacity building and outreach impact (examples: historical counts shown for FY2016–FY2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain Patent and Trademark Operating Reserves
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain two operating reserves—one each for Patents and Trademarks—within acceptable balances (minimum planning level and optimal planning level) to mitigate financial and operational risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserves enable consistent financing of operations and flexibility to respond to workload and revenue volatility; GAO guidance supports maintaining reserves to match fee collections to program costs over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee Schedule Monitoring and Data-Driven Fee Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor and manage USPTO fee schedules and set fees based on forecasts, revenue/spending monitoring, workload trends, and IP environment analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical for sustaining the cost-recovery operating model; requires comprehensive, data-driven decisions informed by available data and capacity assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: IT Modernization Priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: IT investment focus on: movement of applications to the cloud, resilience, and cybersecurity to modernize business IT and retire legacy systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities include migrating off unsupported Windows Server versions, conducting cloud assessments, and engaging contractors for agile development teams to improve time-to-delivery and security posture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal Control Objectives (FMFIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives of internal control under FMFIA: ensure effectiveness and efficiency of operations; reliability of financial reporting; compliance with laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO provides an annual statement of assurance on internal control effectiveness and compliance with FMFIA; assurance is based on evaluations, audits, reconciliations, and external reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Financial Management Improvement Act (FFMIA) Substantial Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial management systems must substantially comply with federal financial management system requirements, federal accounting standards, and the U.S. Standard General Ledger at the transaction level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial compliance is achieved when systems routinely provide reliable/timely financial information, produce reliable financial statements, maintain internal control, and comply with legal/regulatory requirements; USPTO reported substantial compliance for FY2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: FISMA Compliance and Continuous Monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with the Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA) through continuous monitoring, quarterly credentialed compliance and vulnerability scans, monthly OS configuration/patch analyses, and Security Impact Analysis integrated into the SDLC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO states all systems achieved 100% FISMA compliance reporting for FY2021; continuous monitoring and proactive security practices are emphasized to avoid material weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper Payments Risk Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess improper payment risks for all programs and activities annually, per OMB Circular A-123 Appendix C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments include evaluation of control and procurement environments and are updated annually to identify and mitigate improper payment risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt Payment Act Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Make timely payments to vendors and report interest penalties paid for late payments under the Prompt Payment Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO reports percentage of invoices processed without interest penalties and monitors opportunities to improve prompt payment processes (e.g., adoption of electronic invoicing/vendor portal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Debt Collection and Cross-Servicing Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative collection standards per the Debt Collection Improvement Act, including transferring debt more than 120 days old to the Department of the Treasury for cross-servicing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although USPTO has minimal delinquent debt, the statutory standards are observed for any qualifying delinquent balances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Assurance Statement Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Management must provide a statement of assurance regarding internal control over operations, reporting, and compliance with laws and regulations (FMFIA/OMB A‑123 basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement of assurance is supported by internal control programs, audits, independent accountants' opinions, OIG audits, and other assessments; USPTO reported reasonable assurance and no material weaknesses in FY2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Examiner Performance Standards (examination criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent examiners review applications to determine whether the claimed invention is eligible for patent protection, useful, adequately disclosed, and clearly defined; they compare claims to technical information to determine novelty and non-obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners also respond to appeal briefs, prepare PCT preliminary examination reports, and participate in policy development, education, and international cooperation; quality and timeliness metrics track examiner performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Examination Standards (registrability determinations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark examining attorneys search for confusingly similar pending or registered marks, prepare communications with applicants, approve applications for publication, examine statements of use under section 1(b), and evaluate maintenance documents and renewals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These activities form the core registrability determinations under the Trademark Act and are assessed through pendency, compliance, and quality measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPIA Capacity Building and International Engagement Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: OPIA responsibilities: provide capacity building programs on IP protection and enforcement, lead WIPO negotiations, advise on IP provisions of free trade agreements, manage the IP Attaché Program, engage with Congress/federal agencies, and conduct empirical studies of IP impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance measured by training counts, progress in prioritized countries, legislative and international engagement outcomes, and empirical research outputs.
